_comment: 🎬️ ✳️any owns no mutation any more: the eight direct semantic vocabulary entries (six step-node kinds, two dependency-edge kinds) moved to 🪜️step and 🔗️dependency (ticket 26/09/02/SEPARATE-ARTIFACT-STANDARD-SUBSET-IMPLEMENTATIONS-AND-FIXTURE-TEST-EVERY-MUTATION) so each has a real, non-wildcard owner. This contribution keeps the shared io codecs, the whole-document schema/snapshot/diff/editor/viewer surface, and the two capability oracles below — `csv-rfc4180-reader` and the `sequence-1-mutate-uncarried` no-oracle decision both apply registry-wide by capability, not by subset, so neither moves with the mutations that reference them.

oracles.rationale:
📊️ A QUALIFYING CARRIER ORACLE FOR EXACTLY FOUR OF THIS SUBSET'S EIGHT KINDS, AND THE SCOPE IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE REGISTRATION.

What makes it qualify at all is that this subset's csv export is REAL, which was established by reading the serializer body rather than the directory tree. `🚪️io/📤️export/🧵️serializers/🗿️artifacts/📊️csv/🔖️rfc4180/✳️any/🦀️.rs` builds one `CsvRecord` per step — `[id, kind, JSON-encoded params]` — through real row logic, and the second hop `stdio.csv`'s `encode_csv` emits genuine RFC 4180 text. That distinction is not cosmetic here: 80 serializers elsewhere in this repository return `print_dsl(snapshot).into_bytes()` under a standard format's extension, and a third-party reader handed those bytes would be parsing this repository's own DSL text, not the format it claims. Those are refused registration for that reason and flagged by the `stub-serializer` gate. This one is not one of them.

WHAT IT DISCHARGES. `create-step`, `delete-step` and `duplicate-step` add or remove a row a foreign parser counts and reads; `edit-step-params` rewrites the JSON-encoded params column of an identified row. For these four the reader is a genuinely independent producer of the fact under test — it re-derives the row set from bytes without consulting our snapshot type, so a bug in our mutation surfaces as a row disagreement rather than as two halves of this repository agreeing with each other.

WHAT IT CANNOT DISCHARGE, STATED AS A LIMIT AND NOT AS A GAP TO BE PAPERED OVER. `move-step` and `change-step-collapsed` write `x`/`y` and a UI collapse flag; `connect-steps` and `disconnect-steps` write `edges`. The carrier encodes none of them — a flat grid has no edge concept, and the serializer says so in its own header comment. A reader cannot witness a change to something the bytes never carried, so those four kinds carry no `oracleRequirement` discharged by this entry and remain owed a qualifying reference. Registering this oracle against all eight would have produced four green results that prove nothing, which is the precise failure mode Protocol v2's per-mutation requirement exists to prevent.

noOracleDecisions.rationale:
PARTIALLY SUPERSEDED by the `csv-rfc4180-reader` registration, which discharges `create-step`, `delete-step`, `duplicate-step` and `edit-step-params` through this subset's real RFC 4180 export. This decision now stands only for `move-step`, `change-step-collapsed`, `connect-steps` and `disconnect-steps`, whose written fields (x/y, the collapse flag, and `edges`) no exported carrier encodes.

The survey this decision already carries is kept: the BPMN and Graphviz readers are named and declined on the substantive ground that neither models this graph. THAT SURVEY STANDS, AND IT IS NOT WHAT THIS DECISION NOW RESTS ON. Surveying and declining a third-party LIBRARY is a different judgement from declining a SECOND IMPLEMENTATION, and until this re-examination that is the only judgement this decision had ever made. The sentence it used to lean on — that this subset's own shape IS its specification and so not a fact an external implementation could confirm or refute — is refuted inside this repository: `mutate-puzzle-2d-1` and `mutate-puzzle-3d-1`, whose documents carry ports inside nodes and cascade on delete, took Python second implementations over this same `.dsl.semio` carrier, from the same kind of committed material, and between them they surfaced findings no single-implementation case could produce. So THIS DECISION IS A DEBT, NOT A JUDGEMENT, and it is recorded as one here rather than left reading as a verdict.

WHAT A SECOND IMPLEMENTATION HERE WOULD BE WRITTEN FROM: `../🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🔣️.json` for the document's members, the rules of `.🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️08/☀️12/SEMANTIC-MUTATIONS-OVERHAUL/📓️derivation-rules.md` that this vocabulary was derived by, and the eight committed `(before, mutation, after, outcome)` specification vectors under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<kind>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/`. The nearest transferable recipe is `mutate-puzzle-2d-1`: an id-keyed step collection with a sibling edge collection.

WHAT BLOCKS IT TODAY, precisely. This case's committed specification vectors are NOT declared as `asset://` fixtures. Its `Examples` table carries the payloads inline, and the Rust adapter reaches the committed `(before, mutation, after, outcome)` files through `include_str!` instead. Two consequences follow: the execution plan does not pin those files' digests, so a silently edited vector changes the result rather than the plan; and a Python reference cannot read them at all, because the Python host resolves a fixture only through the plan and raises on an undeclared URI. Declaring them — the shape `mutate-program-1`, `mutate-note-1` and `mutate-block-3d-1` already use — is the one edit that unblocks this case, and it strengthens the case whether or not a reference follows. AND, SEPARATELY, `identity-round-trip` WOULD STILL BE REFUSED. This subset's committed snapshot text grammar is the repository-wide PLACEHOLDER: its whole body is `payload = OCTET+` and its header production declares `"schema" SP "stdio.json"`, which the committed artifact contradicts on its own first line. A second reader cannot parse what no document describes — the finding `mutate-iso16757-1`, `mutate-vdi3805-1`, `mutate-program-1` and `mutate-writer-1` all report against their own subsets.

WHAT IS ASSERTED IN THE MEANTIME is unchanged and is listed in `substitutes`: the committed specification vectors, replayed end to end through the platform, and the metamorphic laws the subject handler asserts in role. The ceiling on all of it is unchanged too and is worth restating: no second producer runs beside them, so a mistake shared by the handcrafted vector and the production code passes unseen. 🩹️ NARROWED (ticket SEPARATE-ARTIFACT-STANDARD-SUBSET-IMPLEMENTATIONS-AND-FIXTURE-TEST-EVERY-MUTATION, shard A10): every capability this decision used to list is now either genuinely discharged by a registered qualifying oracle elsewhere in this subset tree, or genuinely required by a real mutation with none registered — and a no-oracle decision may never claim the latter, since that would make an open oracle gap look handled. `capabilities` is now empty; the analysis above is kept as the historical record of how this decision's scope narrowed.
